text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your current symptoms, specifically regarding the increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, and tell me about your recent episodes of pain with urination. Also, could you clarify the history of the painful, swollen left ankle you mentioned?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (formerly Reiter's syndrome).

The combination of asymmetric oligoarthritis affecting the lower extremities (ankle and knee), urethritis (painful urination), and a history of recent sexual activity with inconsistent condom use is highly suggestive of Reactive Arthritis. Given the patient's age and the specific constellation of symptoms, this diagnosis is supported by the clinical presentation even without further testing at this moment.
